sectors.theme: Data-centre power demand is quantified (8.39GW peak by 2030, 12.3GW approved) as a Data Centre Bill heads to Cabinet in 2027; DNB is off the government's books

items.headline: Peninsular data-centre peak power demand is projected at 8.39GW by 2030 (Johor 4.42GW, Selangor 1.48GW), versus 6.04GW of grid supply for the 45 data centres now operating
items.detail: In a parliamentary reply, the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (PETRA) said 45 data centres were operational in Peninsular Malaysia as of August 2026, with 6.04GW of electricity supply capacity provided by TNB through the national grid. Peak demand from the industry is projected at 8.39GW by 2030 on current supply-planning estimates, led by Johor (4.42GW) and Selangor (1.48GW). Projected data-centre water demand in Selangor and Johor is 389.04 million litres a day (MLD) by 2030, against actual reported consumption of 63.90 MLD today. NST separately reports that data-centre projects had secured approval for 12.3GW of electricity supply capacity as of August; Minister Fadillah Yusof said grid and generation will be expanded in phases and that the extra costs of data-centre demand should not be unfairly passed on to other consumers.
items.soWhat: Approved supply (12.3GW) already exceeds the 2030 peak-demand forecast (8.39GW), so the bottleneck is delivery of grid and water infrastructure in Johor and Selangor, and who pays for it.
items.opportunity: Substation, transmission, water-supply and cable works around Johor and Selangor data-centre clusters.
items.watchOut: Projected demand implies water use rising about sixfold from today's 63.90 MLD (computed). The NST body was read only as a syndicated summary (curl and fetch return the headline only).
items.note: Follows the 16 Oct edition (ai-1) on data centres funding their own grid upgrades and the 19 Oct item on off-grid power conditions.

items.headline: Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill to go to Cabinet in 2027, agreed at the NEAC meeting chaired by the PM, to align data-centre growth with energy and water capacity
items.detail: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the National Economic Action Council (NEAC/MTEN) agreed on Monday to draft the Bill after the Digital Ministry presented a National Strategic Direction Towards Sustainable Data Centre Development. Aims: address utility constraints, avoid environmental imbalances and ensure data-centre investment creates spillovers for the local digital ecosystem. The Edge notes data centres are about a tenth of Malaysia's energy consumption, possibly a third by 2035; that power for data centres will be unsubsidised and ring-fenced from other users; that a task force set at least 30% local sourcing of components; and that 27 projects worth an estimated RM225.97bil were approved up to July. The NEAC also told four ministries (KPKT, MITI, MOSTI, Human Resources) to adopt a Circular Economy Framework.
items.soWhat: Data-centre approvals are moving from task-force conditions to legislation, so investors should expect binding utility, local-content and spillover rules from 2027.
items.opportunity: Local suppliers in construction, engineering, cooling and electrical equipment, given the 30% local-sourcing floor.
items.watchOut: The Bill's text, thresholds and timing beyond 'next year' were not disclosed; projects approved now may face retrofit conditions.
items.note: Also reported by Malay Mail, Bernama and EdgeProp (19 Oct). The 27 projects/RM225.97bil figure was in the 14 Oct edition and is context only.

items.headline: DNB completes a RM5.2bil syndicated Islamic refinancing, cutting the government's financial exposure to zero ahead of equal ownership by CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL Power
items.detail: The facility, completed on 29 Sept with Maybank IB (lead arranger), AmInvestment Bank, CIMB Islamic, RHB Islamic and UOB Malaysia, refinanced DNB's government-guaranteed revolving credit facility. Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said the government no longer has any liability in DNB as at end-September and ruled out further state support. MOF Inc will exit as an ordinary shareholder but keep a special share. DNB now holds its full 100MHz of 3.3-3.4GHz spectrum, and its entire 240MHz holding was converted to a spectrum assignment from 1 Oct. CEO Azman Ismail said debt service will rely on access-agreement revenue from the telcos and that DNB will push 5G use among businesses and industries.
items.soWhat: Malaysia's first 5G network now stands on commercial funding and telco ownership, which shifts 5G economics onto CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL Power and their enterprise sales.
items.opportunity: Enterprise 5G (private networks, industrial use cases) is DNB's stated next growth push.
items.watchOut: Repayment depends on telco access fees and 5G take-up; loan terms and pricing were not disclosed.

items.headline: Singapore neocloud Aolani signs non-binding LOIs for 500MW of AI data-centre capacity in Malaysia from 2H2027, taking its planned Malaysian commitment to up to 580MW
items.detail: Aolani said the Tier III sites, across multiple Malaysian locations, will house purpose-built AI data centres; Aolani will supply AI infrastructure and GPU deployment. It has about 80MW committed in 2026. It cites Malaysia's competitive power costs, available land and government support, and is exploring compute partnerships with Malaysian sovereign AI programmes, enterprises, researchers and start-ups. The letters of intent are non-binding and subject to definitive agreements. Counterparties and sites were not named.
items.soWhat: A large GPU tenant pipeline for Malaysian data-centre landlords, but on non-binding terms and dependent on the power approvals described in ai-1 and ai-2.
items.watchOut: Non-binding LOIs; no named landlords, sites, capex or power arrangements.

sectors.theme: KPKT reports progress on sick projects but 668 delayed, sick or abandoned projects remain; strong take-up for mid-priced Setapak high-rise

items.headline: Peninsular Malaysia still has 668 delayed, sick or abandoned private housing projects (about 108,760 units) as at 31 Aug, KPKT data show, including 278 sick projects worth RM38.02bil GDV
items.detail: KPKT's backlog as at 31 Aug 2026: 128 delayed projects (29,048 units, RM24.39bil GDV), 278 sick projects (40,818 units, RM38.02bil), 99 licensed abandoned projects (28,289 units, RM15.40bil) and 163 unlicensed abandoned projects (10,605 units). KPKT made 33 working visits to delayed and sick projects to August, and 23 of those projects have since obtained their CCC. Deputy Minister Aiman Athirah Sabu said Residensi Hektar Gombak (92.67% complete) should finish in 1Q2027, with vacant possession in 2Q2027, after a stakeholder recovery plan backed by financing from local banks. Rehabilitation since 2023 (1,726 projects, RM158.16bil GDV) breaks down as 1,542 sick projects obtained their CCC (163,621 units, RM115.74bil GDV), 147 sick projects (29,900 units, RM40.92bil) returned to satisfactory progress and 37 abandoned projects (6,122 units, RM1.504bil) resolved.
items.soWhat: Rescue work is clearing the backlog, but about RM78bil of GDV (computed, excluding unlicensed projects) is still stuck, keeping buyer-protection policy and rescue-contractor opportunities in play.
items.opportunity: Rescue development and completion contracts for stalled projects coordinated by KPKT's task force (TFST).
items.watchOut: 668 projects and 108,760 units are computed sums of the four categories. GDV for unlicensed projects was not given.
items.note: The 1,726 rehabilitated projects (RM158.16bil GDV) were covered in the 14 Oct edition; the backlog breakdown and the Hektar Gombak timeline are new. Bernama also reported the Hektar Gombak timeline (19 Oct, 12:09).

items.headline: Mah Sing's M Mira in Setapak hits 93% take-up for Phase 1 and opens Phase 2: 633 units of 800-1,050 sq ft from RM474,000
items.detail: The high-rise in Wangsa Maju, Setapak, is 650m from Sri Rampai LRT and 820m from Wangsa Maju LRT, with provisional GreenRE Silver certification. Founder Leong Hoy Kum said the group is still buying land in strategic locations and sees digital infrastructure as a potential secondary growth engine, exploring related utility and infrastructure support solutions.
items.soWhat: Transit-linked, sub-RM500,000 stock in mature KL suburbs is still selling quickly, even as the overall overhang rises.
items.watchOut: Take-up is company-reported; the Phase 1 unit count was not given separately.

items.headline: Putrajaya urges states to copy Pahang's low-cost homes with built-in solar: RM10,000 of PV added to a RM150,000 house and financed in the RM160,000 mortgage
items.detail: Deputy Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister Abdul Rahman Mohamad told the Dewan Rakyat there is no federal solar-installation aid for low-income households yet, but states can follow Pahang, where new low-cost housing includes solar PV in the purchase price. Federal support: RM150mil for SuRIA Home (rebate of RM600 per kWac, up to RM3,000 per household for 5kWac, targeting 45,000-50,000 households), and NUR MADANI rebates of RM200 for 4- or 5-star air-conditioners and refrigerators.
items.soWhat: Bundling solar into affordable-home pricing could become a state-housing specification, and that adds cost and a financing step for developers and buyers.
items.opportunity: Developers and solar installers packaging rooftop PV into affordable and mid-market launches; SuRIA rebates lower the buyer's cost.
items.watchOut: This is a suggestion to states, not a requirement; it adds about 6.7% (computed) to the house price in the Pahang example.

items.headline: Sime Darby Property calls a 3 Nov EGM to approve buying 556.96 acres of Kulai land from SD Guthrie for RM418.5mil (RM17.25 psf, 4.23% below the RM437mil valuation) for a RM3bil-GDV JS-SEZ township
items.detail: The circular dated 19 Oct sets the EGM for 3 Nov at 2.30pm. The freehold land sits in Mukim Senai, Kulai, within Flagship Zone F (Kulai-Sedenak) of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, and is zoned residential but still planted with oil palms (92.60% of the planted area is 19 years or older). RM75.3mil (18%) was paid when the SPA was signed on 11 Aug. The balance is due on completion, expected in 2Q2027, from internal funds and/or borrowings; if fully debt-funded, net gearing rises from 0.36 times to 0.40 times. Planning applications are due in 1Q2027, the first phase launches in 2028, and the township of landed homes and commercial lots is to be built out over 10-15 years. It is a related-party deal (ASB is a major shareholder of both companies); independent adviser Alliance Islamic Bank calls it fair and reasonable. SD Guthrie's shareholders approved the sale on 15 Oct with 99.9989% of votes, and it books a net gain of about RM373.36mil.
items.soWhat: A top-tier developer is adding a large landed township in the Kulai-Senai corridor near Bandar Putra and data-centre parks, with launches from 2028. RM17.25 psf is a fresh price reference for residential-zoned plantation land in the JS-SEZ.
items.opportunity: Planters are selling mature estates near Johor growth corridors, so more land could come to market at similar prices.
items.watchOut: Not new: the deal was signed on 11 Aug, and this circular is the procedural step. More landed supply in Kulai from 2028 will compete for buyers.
items.note: Not in the 14-19 Oct editions. The SPA dates from 11 Aug (company press release) and SD Guthrie's EGM was on 15 Oct (EdgeProp, 16 Oct). New in the window: Sime Darby Property's own circular (Bursa ann 3715941), with the EGM date, valuation, funding and gearing figures. Figures taken from the circular PDF. The 17 Oct edition saw a title-only Sime Darby Property EGM notice and did not itemise it.

sectors.theme: Watchlist win for GDB in Sarawak; Penang secures RM33.22bil federal pipeline; Sabah Pan Borneo now faces a PAC probe; ECRL targets a 12 Dec opening

items.headline: GDB wins a RM119mil (RM118.99mil) subcontract for the National Flood Forecasting and Warning Programme Phase 3 in Sarawak, lifting year-to-date wins to RM795.3mil
items.detail: GDB Infra Sdn Bhd received the subcontract from main contractor I-Ilham Corporation Sdn Bhd, with completion due 29 Nov 2029. It is GDB's fourth infrastructure contract in Sarawak, bringing its construction value in the state to RM355.9mil. The company says the win keeps it on track for its RM1bil FY2026 order-book target, and its tender book was RM4.3bil as at 13 Oct, spanning industrial, data-centre, commercial, mixed-use, infrastructure and residential work. GDB shares closed 3.70% higher at 42 sen (market cap RM433.13mil).
items.soWhat: GDB is diversifying from Klang Valley building jobs into East Malaysian flood and water infrastructure, which is funded by federal flood-mitigation spending.
items.opportunity: Federal flood-forecasting and mitigation programmes in Sarawak are generating subcontract packages.
items.watchOut: A subcontract, so margins depend on the main contractor's terms; the RM1bil target is the company's own.
items.note: Bursa filing 19 Oct (ann 3716263): GDB Infra accepted the subcontract (RM118,992,249.32) on 2 Aug 2026, but disclosure was withheld until I-Ilham cleared it on 19 Oct, so the award is newly disclosed rather than newly won. Also reported by Business Today. GDB's executive director's share purchase was in the 17 Oct edition (con-4).

items.headline: Parliament's PAC opens a probe into Sabah's Pan Borneo Highway Phase 1: RM10.547bil spent of RM11.153bil allocated, with 57 variation orders worth RM513.99mil approved beyond authorised limits
items.detail: PAC chair Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the issues go beyond construction delays to governance and accountability; witnesses from the Works Ministry and JKR will be called, and any misconduct will be referred to the MACC and police. The Auditor-General also found RM163.64mil of interim payments made without formal contracts, and Phase 1A's projected cost up RM987mil to RM11.323bil, above the RM10.336bil ceiling. Only 4 of 35 packages are complete and the deadline is now 2030. Separately, Deputy Works Minister Ahmad Maslan denied payment delays: Phase 1A is at 89.54% physical progress against 96.23% scheduled (payments 88.78%), while Phase 1B is at 25.53% against 24.76% scheduled. He blamed contractor issues and the 2019 switch from the PDP model, and said project cost had risen to RM24.89bil from RM12.86bil.
items.soWhat: Contractors and consultants on Sabah Pan Borneo now face a parliamentary inquiry with possible enforcement referrals, and that could slow payments and variation approvals across the remaining packages.
items.watchOut: The cost figures differ by source: The Edge cites a total contract cost of RM18.394bil (from RM17.91bil), while the ministry cites a project cost of RM24.89bil (from RM12.86bil). The bases are not explained.
items.note: Follows the 19 Oct edition (con-1) on package handovers. What is new is the PAC probe and the ministry's progress and payment figures.

items.headline: Penang gets RM33.22bil for 280 federal projects under the 13MP's Second Rolling Plan, with RM2.68bil allocated for 2027 and 44 new projects worth RM578.29mil
items.detail: Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the list has 44 new and 236 ongoing projects. The new projects have RM63.71mil allocated for 2027. Four state priority projects worth RM96.95mil were approved (RM2.2mil for 2027): the Sungai Keluang Ubi flood mitigation scheme, the Jalan Bukit Tambun FT149 upgrade, the Sungai Perai flood mitigation scheme (Phase 2) and groundwater mapping. The state is also pursuing a Penang Technology Financial Centre, which it projects would add RM12.1bil to GDP and 71,000 jobs over 15 years.
items.soWhat: Penang's federal works pipeline is large but back-loaded: only about 8% (computed) of the RM33.22bil is funded for 2027, so tender timing matters for contractors.
items.opportunity: Flood-mitigation and road-upgrade tenders in Seberang Perai.
items.watchOut: Most of the value is in ongoing projects; new-project allocations for 2027 are small (RM63.71mil).

items.headline: ECRL could open on 12 Dec, with Gombak-Kota Bharu fares from RM125 (Transit) and RM147 (Express); MRL targets 1.4mil passengers in 2027 and 70% of revenue from cargo once freight starts in 2028
items.detail: MRL CEO Darwis Abdul Razak said the fault-free run starts on 23 Oct, with trial operations in November and ticket sales from mid-November, subject to safety approvals. Cabinet approved dynamic fares on 16 Oct (mid-range Transit RM156). Fares to Kuala Terengganu start at RM95/RM110 and to KotaSAS at RM60/RM68. The railway will run 10 EMU sets, with 12 daily services Monday-Thursday and 16 Friday-Sunday, on about 2.2mil seats in 2027 at a roughly 60% load factor. The project cost about RM52.3bil. Phase 2 will add Serendah, Puncak Alam, Kapar and Jalan Kastam stations towards Port Klang.
items.soWhat: The 523km line becomes an operating asset this year, which brings forward property and logistics plays around its 16 Phase 1 stations and the 2028 freight link to Port Klang.
items.opportunity: Station-area development, last-mile transport and east-coast tourism; cargo transfer at Temerloh and Serendah from 2028.
items.watchOut: Opening is subject to safety approvals. Passenger revenue alone will not cover a RM52.3bil project, as MRL acknowledges.
items.note: Also reported by Malay Mail and Bernama (19 Oct).

items.headline: Putrajaya aims to fit Smart Highway technology, including multi-lane free flow (MLFF) tolling, to at least 50% of Malaysia's 34 expressways
items.detail: Works Minister Alexander Nanta Linggi, at the ITS World Congress in Gangneung, South Korea, listed AI and smart CCTV, incident early-warning systems, solar lighting, mobility apps and EV charging, plus a national intelligent traffic management centre. Highway concessionaires and industry partners are refining a business-to-business MLFF model under Malaysian Highway Authority oversight. Technical, operational and legal preparations are being finalised before the proposal goes to the government for approval.
items.soWhat: MLFF and smart-highway roll-outs open systems-integration, telecoms and civil works for concessionaires and their vendors, but the commercial model is not yet approved.
items.watchOut: Proposal stage only; no timeline, cost or funding split was given.

sectors.theme: Acquisitions lift KIP REIT's income but dilute per-unit earnings

items.headline: KIP REIT's 1Q net property income rises 18% to RM34.95mil on new retail and industrial assets, but earnings per unit fall to 1.49 sen from 1.87 sen after 200mil new units
items.detail: Revenue rose almost 20% to RM48.75mil (from RM40.77mil) in the quarter to 30 Sept, helped by assets acquired in Selangor, Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Sarawak. EPU fell because a private placement added 200mil units. No distribution was declared for the quarter, though an advance income distribution of 0.82 sen was paid in September. The REIT holds 20 properties (six industrial) worth over RM2bil. CEO Valerie Ong said KIPMall Setapak, acquired in September, will contribute its first full quarter now. Managers expect stable performance through FY2027.
items.soWhat: Neighbourhood-mall REITs are still growing by acquisition, but unitholders need the new assets to lift income per unit, not just total income.
items.watchOut: Per-unit earnings are down 20% (computed) despite higher income.

items.headline: 1 Utama City Group's 215m-tall The Capitol in Bandar Utama, with two Grade A office towers above a six-level retail podium, soft-opens on 16 Nov
items.detail: The integrated development sits next to LRT3's BU11 station. Confirmed tenants include F&B names (Kiwami Ramen & Gyoza Bar, Bean Brothers, Galito's, Fowlboys Diner, Qra, and SE'INDONESIA in its Malaysian debut), Common Ground coworking, Cutie Cottage childcare, Guardian and PUMP Fitness. Health Capitol will house more than 120 medical practitioners. A Level 16 recreational floor and a 10,000 sq ft SkyHall event space open in 2Q2027. It targets GreenRE Platinum certification.
items.soWhat: New retail and Grade A office supply in Bandar Utama-Damansara, built around healthcare, F&B and services, competes for tenants and footfall with nearby malls and offices.
items.opportunity: Healthcare and services anchors, plus a transit link, are a template for refreshing older retail assets.
items.watchOut: No NLA, occupancy or rent figures were disclosed, and only a first batch of tenants is confirmed.
items.note: The Star, 19 Oct 4:32pm (company statement). Not in the 14-19 Oct editions.

sectors.theme: CPO steady near RM4,500-4,700 as high stocks cap gains; MP calls for cooking-oil subsidy to be phased out

items.headline: CPO futures end mixed: November down RM21 to RM4,515/t and December down RM10 to RM4,666/t, as high inventories offset Indian pre-Deepavali demand
items.detail: January slipped RM3 to RM4,766, while February to April rose RM5-10 (April RM4,993). Volume fell to 106,846 lots from 133,428, and open interest to 332,357 from 339,364. Physical November South rose RM30 to RM4,530. Iceberg X trader David Ng sees support at RM4,600 and resistance at RM4,850. Reuters cited a trader saying prices were also pressured by market speculation that Malaysia is weighing a waiver of CPO export taxes to cut stocks, and reported that Malaysia's agricultural exports fell 5.7% in September on lower palm shipments.
items.soWhat: Elevated domestic stocks are capping prices; any export-tax relief (speculation only) would be a policy lever to watch for planters' margins.
items.watchOut: The export-tax waiver is unconfirmed market speculation reported by a trader, not a government statement.
items.note: Follows the 18 Oct edition (pl-1) weekly close of RM4,536 for November.

items.headline: Gopeng MP urges a phase-out of the cooking oil price stabilisation scheme (COSS), which cost RM10.879bil in 2019-2025 (about RM1.55bil a year), with 67% of its quota held by foreign-owned firms
items.detail: Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng), debating Budget 2027, cited a July PAC report on quota oversupply, subsidy management and the transparency of payments to refiners and packers. He proposed redirecting the money to targeted aid such as SARA. He also flagged the RM380bil 2027 revenue projection, a RM10bil cut to operating spending this year and debt service of about RM61bil next year.
items.soWhat: If COSS is wound down, refiners and packers that rely on subsidised-quota volumes lose a volume and margin buffer, and the government gains about RM1.5bil a year of fiscal room.
items.watchOut: This is a backbench proposal, not government policy.

items.headline: Growers' group MPOA says October palm output may set a monthly record and 2026 could match or beat 2025's record 20.28mil tonnes, but 2027 faces an 18,000-harvester shortage and a lagged El Niño
items.detail: MPOA head Roslin Azmy Hassan (interview with Bloomberg) expects output to peak in October and ease in November-December. The current October record is 2.04mil tonnes, set last year. September output was already an all-time high of 2.12mil tonnes, up 16% month on month, as replanted areas mature. In 2027, the shortage of about 18,000 harvesters could leave 8.6mil tonnes of fresh fruit bunches uncollected (about RM8bil of lost revenue), and the impact of El Niño is expected from 2H2027. A planned minimum-wage rise next year adds to production costs that are already about RM2,600-3,000 a tonne. Palm oil has risen 18% in 2026, and benchmark futures touched RM5,049 in mid-September.
items.soWhat: Planters get a strong 4Q volume quarter, but the 2027 supply outlook turns on labour quotas and weather, which supports prices more than volumes.
items.opportunity: Estates with younger, replanted palms and mechanised harvesting gain the most from the peak and suffer least from the labour gap.
items.watchOut: This is an industry body's forecast, not official data. Record stocks (3.51mil tonnes in September, 14 Oct edition) still cap near-term prices.
items.note: Industry view (MPOA), via Bloomberg in The Star (19 Oct, 8:56pm). September output and stocks were in the 14 Oct edition. What is new is the October-record call, the full-year outlook and the 2027 labour and El Niño risk.

sectors.theme: Exports beat forecasts and CPI cools to 1.8%, splitting views on a 5 Nov hike; Japanese insurer eyes LPI; Zetrix nears its sukuk deadline

items.headline: September exports jump 54.5% to RM215.1bil, a five-year high (E&E +68%), beating the 39.9% consensus; RHB raises its 2026 export forecast to 34.4% from 21.7%
items.detail: MITI data: imports rose 52.7% to RM181.4bil (consensus 39%), leaving a RM33.7bil trade surplus. E&E, over half of exports, set a monthly record; optical and scientific equipment also hit a record. Petroleum products rose 33% and LNG 46%. Exports to the US rose 72% and to China 52%. Intermediate-goods imports rose 69.6% to RM92.1bil. Analyst views: MBSB IB raised its 2026 export forecast to 32%; BIMB keeps 23.4% but expects growth to moderate in 4Q2026 and into 2027; Pantheon says base effects should eventually temper E&E's contribution. CGS International keeps its 2026 GDP forecast at 5.5%, citing a record 5.3% year-on-year working-capital loan growth in August.
items.soWhat: The AI-driven trade surge is still accelerating, which supports corporate earnings, the ringgit and industrial demand into year-end, though analysts expect the pace to slow from 4Q.
items.watchOut: MITI flags shifting trade policies and West Asia conflicts; economists expect base effects to slow growth in 4Q.
items.note: Analyst forecasts are labelled as such. Business Today reports OCBC sees 3Q GDP above 5.3% (headline only; not read).

items.headline: September CPI eases to 1.8% (core 1.7%), below the 1.9% consensus: Pantheon sees a long OPR hold at 2.75%, RHB a 25bp hike in 1H2027 and UOB a move as early as 5 Nov
items.detail: DOSM data: CPI rose 0.1% month on month (0.3% in August). Housing, water, electricity, gas and fuels inflation eased to 1.4% from 2.1% after an automatic fuel adjustment revision; transport rose to 2.5% from 2% (personal transport operation +2.7%). Food and beverages rose 1.8%. September is the last CPI print before BNM's 5 Nov decision. MOF projects 1.5-2.5% inflation for 2026 and 1.8-2.8% for 2027. RHB flags El Nino risks to rice and oil-palm yields.
items.soWhat: Funding-cost planning should allow for both a hold and a 25bp rise around the 5 Nov MPC: inflation is benign, but growth and an expansionary budget keep hike calls alive.
items.watchOut: Economists' rate calls diverge; UOB cites stronger 3Q growth and Budget 2027 stimulus.
items.note: Analyst views. TMR also headlined UOB's call for a hike as early as November.

items.headline: Japan's MS&AD is said to be exploring a takeover of LPI Capital (about RM5bil market cap); CIMB Securities estimates Public Bank could book a RM521mil gain on its 44.15% stake
items.detail: Bloomberg, citing unnamed people, said MS&AD is working with advisers, considerations may not lead to a deal and other bidders could emerge; all parties declined to comment or did not respond. Public Bank bought the stake in December 2024 for RM1.72bil (RM9.80 a share), and it is now worth about RM2.24bil at RM12.76. CIMB estimates that combining MS&AD's MSIG with LPI's Lonpac would create a general insurer with about 16% market share, ahead of Allianz General's 15%, but says Public Bank would have to weigh losing recurring earnings. CIMB keeps its Buy on Public Bank with a target price cut to RM5.35 from RM5.50; Public Bank fell 2.69% to RM4.70 intraday.
items.soWhat: Another Japanese move on Malaysian general insurance (after Tokio Marine-RHB) points to consolidation, with pricing and partner shifts for corporate insurance buyers.
items.watchOut: Unconfirmed media report; no offer has been made. The gain and market-share figures are CIMB estimates.

items.headline: Zetrix AI scraps its 0.25 sen interim dividend (about RM19.74mil) to conserve cash, as its MD's stake falls to 1.887% three days before the 22 Oct deadline on its RM2bil sukuk covenant
items.detail: The company cited 'unexpected operational expenses'. The dividend was declared on 24 Aug and due on 20 Nov. MD Wong Thean Soon sold another 600,000 shares at 5 sen on 16 Oct and now holds 0.547% directly and 1.34% indirectly; the covenant requires him to remain the largest shareholder. Without a remedy or a holders' waiver, early repayment of RM2bil principal plus RM164.5mil of coupons (RM2.16bil) could be triggered. The shares fell 9.09% to 5 sen, a 14-year low (market cap RM394.9mil). At end-June it had RM541.6mil cash and RM532.88mil in digital assets against RM2.19bil of borrowings, and it owes JPJ RM314mil. Police have recorded statements from 15 people, including 12 JPJ officers, in the related MyEG probe.
items.soWhat: Sukuk holders should prepare for a waiver vote or dissolution event after 22 Oct; the dividend cut signals tight liquidity.
items.watchOut: The cash figure is from end-June; the outcome after 22 Oct is unknown.
items.note: Follows the 19 Oct edition (cf-1, MARC downgrade to BB+IS). What is new is the dividend withdrawal, the further share sale and the probe update. Malay Mail is cited from its feed headline and URL.

items.headline: FBM KLCI drops 12.01 points to 1,595.75, below the 1,600 support level, as foreign institutions extend net selling to four straight weeks (RM270.2mil in the week to 16 Oct)
items.detail: Rakuten Trade's Thong Pak Leng stays cautious but sees value in selected blue chips. MBSB Investment Bank's fund-flow report shows foreign institutions sold on all five days last week (largest outflow RM105.7mil on Monday 12 Oct). By sector, net foreign inflows went to financial services (RM88.5mil), healthcare (RM55.5mil) and transport (RM52.8mil); outflows came from utilities (RM201.3mil), industrial products (RM131.3mil) and plantation (RM75.8mil). Local institutions were net sellers of RM140.3mil, while retail investors bought RM410.5mil, an eighth straight week of net buying. Across eight Asian markets, foreign outflows totalled US$28.32bil, led by Taiwan.
items.soWhat: Weak foreign demand for Malaysian equities makes equity fund-raising and IPO pricing harder near term, despite strong macro data.
items.watchOut: Weekly flow data covers 12-16 Oct; Monday's (19 Oct) flows were not reported in the text read.
items.note: Close per Malay Mail (Bernama copy): down 12.01 points (0.74%) from 1,607.76, with decliners leading 741 to 322 on RM2.38bil turnover; banks led losses (Public Bank -12 sen to RM4.71, Maybank -9 sen to RM9.90). FMT and Business Today also reported the index closing below 1,600.

items.headline: CIMB extends its RM3bil sustainability-linked financing programme to oil-palm and real-estate SMEs, with rebates of up to 0.50% a year for hitting emissions or building-energy targets
items.detail: CIMB Bank and CIMB Islamic introduced new Sustainability-Linked Financing (SLF) structures for businesses, including SMEs, in oil palm (plantations and mills) and real estate, and for firms buying or upgrading properties into green-certified buildings. Rebates are tied to pre-set Sustainability Performance Targets such as GHG reduction; for real estate, Building Energy Intensity (BEI) is an alternative measure. Eligible initiatives include methane capture, biomass use and green vehicles for oil palm, and solar plus battery storage, energy audits and green certification for buildings. An entry-level option rewards SMEs measuring emissions for the first time, with subsidised carbon-measurement tools.
items.soWhat: Green capex on plantations, mills and buildings can now earn a pricing rebate, which lowers the cost of decarbonisation spending and of retrofitting commercial assets.
items.opportunity: Price financing for mill methane capture, rooftop solar and BESS on owned buildings, and green-building upgrades of investment properties, against the up-to-0.50% rebate.
items.watchOut: Rebates depend on meeting and verifying targets; the bank statement gives no programme utilisation figure.
items.note: Bank press statement. Relevant to plantation and property-investment owners as well as financing.

sectors.theme: Car sales up 19% year on year ahead of year-end promotions; RM11bil of cash aid paid out; tiered electricity charges planned from 2027

items.headline: September vehicle sales rise 19% year on year to 69,609 units (down 2.5% from August) as buyers wait for Budget 2027; 9M2026 total industry volume up 4% to 602,633
items.detail: MAA data: passenger vehicle sales rose 21.5% (computed; NST rounds to 21.5%, The Edge to 22%) to 64,835 units, while commercial vehicles fell 7.1% to 4,774. Nine-month passenger sales rose 5% to 564,919 and commercial fell 13% to 37,714. September production rose 10% to 64,482 units. MAA expects October sales to pick up on year-end promotions.
items.soWhat: Car demand is holding up strongly year on year, which supports hire-purchase loan growth into year-end promotions.
items.watchOut: Month on month sales dipped as consumers waited for Budget 2027 measures.
items.note: NST body read via WebFetch.

items.headline: Nearly RM11bil of STR and SARA cash aid was paid out by September from the RM15bil 2026 allocation; monthly SARA utilisation is 99.7% (RM5.2bil spent)
items.detail: In a written parliamentary reply, MOF said RM3.6bil of STR was paid in three phases. Nearly 9mil citizens are eligible for monthly SARA. Under SARA Untuk Semua, more than 20mil citizens (90% of recipients) made purchases worth nearly RM1.9bil. Separately, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said M40 households that lose jobs or income can appeal for a reassessment of aid eligibility at any time; Budget 2027 raises individual tax relief to RM12,000 from RM9,000.
items.soWhat: Cash aid is being spent almost in full at local retailers, which supports mass-market consumption and the repayment capacity of lower-income borrowers.
items.watchOut: An MP has proposed redirecting the cooking-oil subsidy to SARA (pl-2); aid design may shift in Budget 2027 debates.

items.headline: Putrajaya plans a tiered electricity fuel surcharge (AFA) from 2027, as the 800kWh household exemption ends in December; TNB is absorbing an estimated RM120-150mil
items.detail: Deputy Minister Abdul Rahman Mohamad told the Dewan Rakyat that PETRA and the Energy Commission are studying a tiered AFA and an automatic mechanism to protect consumers from surges, amid high fuel costs from the West Asia conflict and hot weather. 8.8mil households use under 800kWh a month and 550,000 use more. The Electricity Industry Fund (KWIE) has subsidised bills since May, and the ministry is concerned its reserves may not be enough.
items.soWhat: Household power bills could rise from January if the exemption lapses before the tiered system is in place, and that squeezes disposable income for heavy users.
items.watchOut: The design and timing of the tiered AFA are not final; the KWIE's capacity is in question.

items.headline: CTOS falls 15.29% to a record-low 36 sen, down 44.19% since its breach disclosure, as EPF, KWAP and Aberdeen cut about 21.57mil shares; Kenanga's worst case puts the FY26 profit hit at RM22mil
items.detail: Bursa filings show only disposals since 23 Sept. KWAP sold 1.77mil shares on 16 Oct (now 8.724%), EPF 1.31mil on 14 Oct (20.43%) and Aberdeen 384,000 on 14 Oct (14.79%), together about 1% of the share capital. Volume was 29.39mil shares, the highest in more than three months. The company's estimate (13 Oct) is a RM12mil profit hit, assuming CTOS Score and CCRIS-related reports return by the third week of October, plus about RM1.3mil for each extra week. Kenanga (analyst view, now Market Perform) assumes an outage to end-December, which raises the hit to RM22mil. RHB keeps a Buy, arguing the sell-off is excessive.
items.soWhat: This is the week the company expected credit-report services back. If they slip further, lenders keep running slower, costlier credit checks, and confidence in the bureau keeps falling.
items.opportunity: Lenders with their own scoring data and alternative bureaux gain relative to CTOS-dependent originators.
items.watchOut: Analysts warn that restored services may not bring volumes back immediately, given customer migration and higher cybersecurity costs.
items.note: Follows the 14 Oct (cf-2) and 16 Oct (cs-1) editions, which reported the breach, the RM12mil estimate and the 42 sen low. What is new is the 36 sen low, the institutional selling and Kenanga's end-December scenario. NST, 19 Oct 23:20; read via the browser sweep and KLSE Screener's copy of the text.

sectors.theme: Data-centre power works and Sarawak's grid build-out feed cable demand; Southern Cable closes its placement

items.headline: Jati Tinggi wins a RM30.1mil contract for two circuits of 275kV underground cable ducting and 11kV temporary power cables for a data centre in Kulai, Johor
items.detail: The EPCC contract went to Jati Tinggi Holding Sdn Bhd from an unnamed Malaysian data-centre infrastructure company and runs to 25 July 2027. Earlier this month, Jati Tinggi won two TNB contracts worth RM15.7mil (underground cable works in Selangor and a submarine power-cable monitoring system in Perlis). Its shares closed at RM1.20 (market cap RM531.51mil).
items.soWhat: Data-centre campuses in Johor are generating high-voltage cable and ducting work beyond TNB's own tenders, which feeds demand for 275kV and 11kV cable suppliers.
items.opportunity: 275kV/11kV cable supply and installation for Johor data-centre connections (see ai-1: Johor peak demand 4.42GW by 2030).
items.watchOut: The customer is unnamed; the contract is small relative to the sector pipeline.

items.headline: Sarawak targets 15,000MW of generation by 2035 (at least 60% renewable) and plans exports of up to 1,000MW to Singapore, now at the submarine-cable survey stage
items.detail: Utility Minister Julaihi Narawi said 3,285MW is being built: Baleh hydro (1,285MW, 4Q2029), Samalaju CCPP (1,500MW; Block 3 of 500MW in 1Q2027 and Blocks 1-2 of 1,000MW in 2Q2027) and Miri CCGT (500MW, 63% complete, 4Q2027). Sarawak exports about 100MW to West Kalimantan and 30MW to Sabah, and plans at least 30MW to Brunei (in negotiation), up to 1,000MW to Singapore and at least 1,000MW to Peninsular Malaysia (early discussions).
items.soWhat: Sarawak's 'Battery of Asean' plan implies large transmission and subsea-cable projects over the next decade, but the export links are still pre-commitment.
items.opportunity: HV transmission and subsea cable supply for the Singapore and Peninsular interconnections, and grid works for Samalaju and Miri.
items.watchOut: The Singapore link is at survey stage and the Peninsular link in early discussions; no contracts have been awarded.

items.headline: Southern Cable ends its private placement at 102,378,500 shares, short of the 10% maximum, and deems it completed
items.detail: A Bursa Malaysia announcement (ann 3716152) by RHB Investment Bank on behalf of the board, dated 19 Oct 2026, says the company decided not to place the remaining shares of its placement of up to 10%, so the placement (first announced on 14 Oct 2025) is deemed completed. Proceeds and pricing were not stated in the announcement.
items.soWhat: The placement overhang is gone; Southern Cable's capital base is now fixed for its next phase.
items.watchOut: Proceeds and use of funds are not stated in the completion notice.
items.note: A separate filing (ann 3716159, notice received 19 Oct) shows EPF bought 430,300 shares on 14 Oct, lifting its direct stake to 70,183,109 shares (5.49%). Both filings were confirmed on the Bursa site and on KLSE Screener.

sectors.theme: Hotel groups lean on Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 with deep discounts; MOF makes no commitment to support AirAsia

items.headline: Berjaya Hospitality signs an MoU with Tourism Malaysia for Visit Malaysia 2026-2027, offering up to 70% off rooms at its 10 Malaysian hotels and resorts (2,974 rooms)
items.detail: BHG will promote Malaysia through its hotels in the UK, the Philippines, Japan, Sri Lanka, the Seychelles, Vietnam and Iceland, join Tourism Malaysia's international sales missions and run familiarisation trips and joint packages. The 'Stay Berjaya, Discover More of Malaysia' offer requires two nights at city hotels or three at resorts, for bookings to 31 Dec 2026 and stays to 30 June 2027. BHG said China contributed more than 16,000 and India more than 45,000 room nights to the group in 2025 (not specified as Malaysia-only).
items.soWhat: Deep discounting by a major operator signals rate pressure in leisure and city hotels, even as Visit Malaysia drives volume.
items.opportunity: Co-marketing with Tourism Malaysia's sales missions for operators with overseas networks.
items.watchOut: Up to 70% discounts may weigh on average room rates; it is an MoU without stated targets.
items.note: CGS International (via Bernama) says Malaysia had 28.8mil tourist arrivals in 8M2026 against the 47mil target for the extended Visit Malaysia campaign (analyst citing Tourism Malaysia).

items.headline: MOF says it has made no commitment to give AirAsia guarantees, loans or public funds, after the airline's latest quarterly loss on jet-fuel costs
items.detail: In a written reply to Wee Ka Siong (BN-Ayer Hitam), MOF said any company's application for support would be judged on national interest, fiscal sustainability and protection of public funds, and that it would not comment on media speculation or figures. It noted AirAsia attributed its losses mainly to the jet-fuel spike from the West Asia conflict, and said it engages regularly with the aviation industry. Bernama recalled that AirAsia said on 19 Sept it had not discussed a bailout and was confident in its liquidity.
items.soWhat: No state backstop is on the table for the main low-cost carrier, so air capacity and fares for inbound tourism depend on AirAsia's own funding as fuel costs stay high.
items.watchOut: Higher fuel costs could lead to capacity cuts on routes that feed Malaysian hotels.
items.note: Also reported by NST, FMT and The Sun (19-20 Oct).

keyTakeaways.headline: Data-centre power is now quantified: 12.3GW of supply approved against an 8.39GW 2030 peak forecast, and a Data Centre Bill goes to Cabinet in 2027
keyTakeaways.soWhat: The constraint has moved from approvals to delivering grid and water capacity in Johor and Selangor, and to who pays. Expect binding rules on utilities, local content and spillovers. Tenant demand is still coming (Aolani's 500MW, non-binding), and cable and substation contractors are already winning work.

keyTakeaways.headline: Exports surge 54.5% to RM215.1bil while CPI cools to 1.8%: the 5 Nov OPR call is now genuinely split
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Strong AI-led trade supports earnings and the ringgit, but economists disagree on rates: Pantheon sees a long hold, RHB a hike in 1H2027 and UOB a move as early as 5 Nov (all analyst views). Plan funding for both outcomes. Foreign investors are still net sellers of Malaysian equities.

keyTakeaways.headline: Construction pipeline widens in Borneo and Penang, but governance risk rises: GDB wins RM119mil in Sarawak while a PAC probe lands on Sabah Pan Borneo
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Watchlist name GDB is winning federally funded flood work (YTD RM795.3mil). Penang has RM33.22bil of federal projects, mostly back-loaded. The PAC inquiry into RM513.99mil of unauthorised variation orders may slow approvals and payments for Pan Borneo contractors.

keyTakeaways.headline: Zetrix AI scraps its dividend days before its 22 Oct sukuk deadline
keyTakeaways.soWhat: The RM19.74mil saving is small against a possible RM2.16bil early-repayment claim. With the MD's stake down to 1.887%, a holders' waiver vote is the likely next step.

keyTakeaways.headline: Consumers: car sales up 19% year on year and RM11bil of cash aid spent, but power bills may rise in 2027
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Car demand and aid spending support hire-purchase and mass-market lending. The tiered fuel surcharge and the end of the 800kWh exemption in December are a cost risk for heavier household users.
